Native reimplementation of d3-scale's core: pure functions mapping an input
  domain to an output range. NOT a JS-interop wrapper around real d3.js —
  every scale here is a from-scratch Clojure(Script) closure.

  Each `*-scale` constructor returns a plain function `(f x)` that maps a
  domain value to a range value. Where an inverse mapping makes sense
  (linear, log) a companion `invert` fn is provided, taking the same domain
  and range args (reversed) so callers don't need a stateful scale object —
  `(invert domain range)` returns a function `(f y)` that maps range back to
  domain. This keeps scales as plain functions rather than objects with
  `:scale`/`:invert` keys, which is more idiomatically Clojure.

(ns kotoba.lang.d3.scale
  "Native reimplementation of d3-scale's core: pure functions mapping an input
  domain to an output range. NOT a JS-interop wrapper around real d3.js —
  every scale here is a from-scratch Clojure(Script) closure.

  Each `*-scale` constructor returns a plain function `(f x)` that maps a
  domain value to a range value. Where an inverse mapping makes sense
  (linear, log) a companion `invert` fn is provided, taking the same domain
  and range args (reversed) so callers don't need a stateful scale object —
  `(invert domain range)` returns a function `(f y)` that maps range back to
  domain. This keeps scales as plain functions rather than objects with
  `:scale`/`:invert` keys, which is more idiomatically Clojure."
  (:refer-clojure :exclude [ext]))

(defn- lerp
  "Linear interpolation: map t in [0 1] to [a b]."
  [a b t]
  (+ a (* t (- b a))))

(defn- normalize
  "Inverse of lerp: map v in [a b] to t in [0 1]. a and b may differ in sign;
  division by zero (a == b) returns 0.0 to avoid NaN propagation."
  [a b v]
  (let [span (- b a)]
    (if (zero? span)
      0.0
      (/ (- v a) span))))

(defn linear-scale
  "Return a function mapping domain [d0 d1] to range [r0 r1] via linear
  interpolation. Extrapolates outside the domain (does not clamp).

    ((linear-scale [0 100] [0 1]) 50) ;=> 1/2"
  [[d0 d1] [r0 r1]]
  (fn [x]
    (lerp r0 r1 (normalize d0 d1 x))))

(defn linear-invert
  "Return the inverse of `(linear-scale [d0 d1] [r0 r1])`: a function mapping
  a range value back to its domain value."
  [[d0 d1] [r0 r1]]
  (fn [y]
    (lerp d0 d1 (normalize r0 r1 y))))

(defn- log
  "Natural log, with an explicit base via change-of-base."
  ([x] #?(:clj (Math/log x) :cljs (js/Math.log x)))
  ([base x] (/ (log x) (log base))))

(defn log-scale
  "Return a function mapping a logarithmic domain [d0 d1] (both positive,
  same sign) to a linear range [r0 r1]. `base` defaults to 10. Values are
  transformed to log-space, then interpolated linearly."
  ([domain range] (log-scale domain range 10))
  ([[d0 d1] [r0 r1] base]
   (let [l0 (log base d0)
         l1 (log base d1)]
     (fn [x]
       (lerp r0 r1 (normalize l0 l1 (log base x)))))))

(defn log-invert
  "Inverse of `(log-scale [d0 d1] [r0 r1] base)`: maps a range value back to
  its domain value."
  ([domain range] (log-invert domain range 10))
  ([[d0 d1] [r0 r1] base]
   (let [l0 (log base d0)
         l1 (log base d1)]
     (fn [y]
       #?(:clj (Math/pow base (lerp l0 l1 (normalize r0 r1 y)))
          :cljs (js/Math.pow base (lerp l0 l1 (normalize r0 r1 y))))))))

(defn ordinal-scale
  "Return a function mapping each value in the discrete `domain` seq to the
  corresponding value in the `range` seq (by position; d3's ordinal/point
  scale without banding math). Values not present in `domain` map to nil
  (mirrors d3's `undefined` for unknown domain values)."
  [domain range]
  (let [m (zipmap domain range)]
    (fn [x] (get m x))))

(defn point-scale
  "≈ d3's scalePoint: evenly space each value of the discrete `domain` seq
  across `[r0 r1]`, inclusive of both endpoints (n=1 domain maps to the
  midpoint). This is the categorical-axis workhorse for bar/axis ticks."
  [domain [r0 r1]]
  (let [n (count domain)
        step (when (> n 1) (/ (- r1 r0) (dec n)))
        positions (if (<= n 1)
                    (repeat n (/ (+ r0 r1) 2))
                    (map #(+ r0 (* step %)) (range n)))]
    (ordinal-scale domain positions)))

(defn band-scale
  "≈ d3's scaleBand: divide `[r0 r1]` into `(count domain)` equal-width bands
  with the given `padding` (0..1, fraction of a band's width reserved as
  inter-band gap, split evenly on both sides of every band). Returns a
  function mapping each domain value to `{:start .. :end .. :width ..}` for
  the left edge, right edge, and width of its band (rather than a bare
  number) since bar charts need the full band, not just a point)."
  ([domain range] (band-scale domain range 0))
  ([domain [r0 r1] padding]
   (let [n (max 1 (count domain))
         total (- r1 r0)
         step (/ total n)
         bandwidth (* step (- 1 padding))
         offset (/ (* step padding) 2)
         m (into {}
                 (map-indexed
                  (fn [i d]
                    (let [start (+ r0 (* step i) offset)]
                      [d {:start start
                          :end (+ start bandwidth)
                          :width bandwidth}]))
                  domain))]
     (fn [x] (get m x)))))
